decisions.name: H.IV.1 Theorem
decisions.reason: Hackman's congruence-class formalism for solutions "belonging to P" is a parallel orbit language. NT-8 fixes Pell-equivalence via powers of the fundamental solution instead of scaffolding a second equivalence framework.
decisions.evidence: The live NT-8 manifest already homes the generalized-orbit route through `def-pell-equivalence-of-generalized-solutions`, `thm-generalized-pell-solutions-have-finitely-many-orbits`, and `cor-one-generalized-pell-solution-gives-infinitely-many`. `research/plan-number-theory-track.md` still describes Hackman H.IV as only the qualified generalized-Pell branch and the batch notes still fix orbit language by powers of `\varepsilon_D`, not by Hackman's separate congruence-class formalism. No current NT-8 item cites or needs a second equivalence framework, so this out-of-scope row stands.

decisions.name: Lemma 16.5
decisions.reason: The design's chosen route proves Artinian implies Noetherian by a nilpotent-radical filtration over a finite product of fields, so this auxiliary zero-product lemma is not scaffolded as its own page item.
decisions.evidence: The live CA-4 scaffold proves `thm-artinian-ring-is-noetherian` via finitely many maximal ideals, nilpotent nilradical, Chinese remainder, and a finite nilpotent filtration; it also scaffolds `thm-chinese-remainder-theorem-for-comaximal-ideals` directly. Milne's Lemma 16.5 is an auxiliary zero-product/product-maximal criterion for a different proof packaging, and no current CA-4 item cites it as a separate result. The out-of-scope decision therefore stands.

decisions.name: Corollary (19.14)
decisions.reason: This is a global finite-module theorem over an Artinian ring, stronger than the local finite-length theorem the page actually homes. The scaffold keeps the local case needed for the truncated examples without adding a separate all-finite-modules Artinian theorem.
decisions.evidence: The current CA-4 page still homes only the local finite-module statement `thm-artinian-local-ring-has-nilpotent-maximal-ideal`, and the B-page module examples are the truncated local computations `ex-artinian-truncated-polynomial-ring` and `ex-length-of-a-truncated-local-module`. Altman-Kleiman Corollary (19.14) is the stronger global theorem for all finite modules over an Artinian ring, and no current manifest item or dependency closure needs that stronger statement. This out-of-scope row stands.

decisions.name: Example 16.9
decisions.reason: The design fixed the zero-dimensional non-Noetherian counterexample as an infinite product of fields, so this alternate single-prime witness is not homed on the companion page.
decisions.evidence: The current B page already uses `ex-zero-dimensional-nonnoetherian-ring` to supply the 'all primes maximal but not Artinian' counterexample, and the live coverage now backs that item with Stacks 15.106's product-of-fields and all-primes-maximal conclusions. `research/frontier-21-batch-3.notes.md` still records the deliberate choice of the infinite-product-of-fields witness over Milne's alternate single-prime example. Example 16.9 is therefore a true alternate witness, not a missing current scaffold item, so this out-of-scope row stands.

decisions.name: Lemma 10.52.4
decisions.reason: This lemma is a one-way finite-length to maximal-ideal-power result. The scaffold does not home that intermediate implication as a separate theorem, and the local finite-length item is proved by the converse local filtration route instead.
decisions.evidence: The current CA-4 manifest already gets the global finite-length equivalence through `thm-artinian-ring-has-finite-length` together with the published theorem `thm-composition-series-iff-noetherian-and-artinian`, while the local finite-length theorem is proved by the explicit `M \supseteq \mathfrak m M \supseteq \cdots` filtration in `thm-artinian-local-ring-has-nilpotent-maximal-ideal`. The batch coverage explicitly treats Stacks Lemma 10.52.4 as the one-way maximal-ideal-power implication, and no current item needs it as a separate bridge. This out-of-scope decision stands.

decisions.name: Lemma 2.1
decisions.reason: This is Conrad's pigeonhole approximation engine for an alternate proof of Lagrange's theorem. NT-8 follows the design's continued-fraction route instead of scaffolding a second existence proof here.
decisions.evidence: The live NT-8 existence theorem `thm-lagrange-existence-for-pell-equation` still depends on the continued-fraction route through `lem-square-root-convergent-norm-identity` and `thm-square-root-continued-fraction-period-structure`, not on a pigeonhole approximation lemma. `research/plan-number-theory-track.md` still describes NT-8's route as the continued-fraction existence proof, while the Conrad II harvest keeps Theorem 2.3 but leaves Lemma 2.1 outside scope as an alternate engine. Since the current page already closes without a second proof of Lagrange's theorem, this out-of-scope row stands.

decisions.name: Exercise (19.4)
decisions.reason: This exercise gives the support-based criterion for finite length over a Noetherian ring, but the page keeps the ring-theoretic Artinian criterion and the local finite-length theorem instead of opening a second finite-length criterion for finite modules.

No current item uses a support-based finite-length criterion for finite modules. Exercise (19.4) is therefore an honest extra criterion beyond the page's ring-theoretic route, and the out-of-scope decision stands.
